# Lab 8.1: Create a Dataform Repository & Workspace

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a Dataform repository and a development workspace, and give the Dataform service account the BigQuery permissions it needs.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Grant BigQuery roles to the Dataform service agent.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable dataform.googleapis.com
PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format="value(projectNumber)")
DF_SA=service-$PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-dataform.iam.gserviceaccount.com
for ROLE in roles/bigquery.dataEditor roles/bigquery.jobUser roles/bigquery.dataViewer; do
  gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member=serviceAccount:$DF_SA --role=$ROLE --quiet
done</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Create the repository.** In BigQuery click **Dataform → Create repository**:
   - **Repository ID**: `bq-course-dataform`
   - **Region**: `us-central1`
   - **Service account**: the default Dataform service account

3. **[CLI] Confirm it exists.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  "https://dataform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/repositories" \
  | grep '"name"'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Create a development workspace.** Open the repository → **Create development workspace** → name it `dev-ankit`. Open it and click **Initialize workspace**.

5. **[Console] Look at the files.** The workspace now has:
   - `workflow_settings.yaml`: default project, dataset and location
   - `definitions/`: your SQLX files
   - `includes/`: shared JavaScript

   Edit `workflow_settings.yaml`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • YAML
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">defaultProject: YOUR_PROJECT
defaultLocation: US
defaultDataset: lab08
defaultAssertionDataset: lab08_assertions
dataformCoreVersion: 3.0.0</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Repository | Holds the code, one per project or team |
| Workspace | Your private copy, like a Git branch |
| Service account | Runs the SQL in BigQuery |
| Defaults | Dataset `lab08` in `US` |
